source_inventory.fact: A missing unit cell is built by folding init over session.snapshotEvents(). This handles a unit registered after events flowed or a session created before the registry, but it is a synchronous complete-history read owned by the projection registry.

An existing cell advances by looking up every missing sequence with session.eventAt(). The loop preserves a contiguous watermark and throws on a gap, but it assumes the complete log remains synchronously resident.

The eager event drive builds a late cell by folding the prefix before the delivered event, then applies that event. Removing this read without a lifecycle baseline would silently lose prior state or make the next event non-contiguous.

Constructor seeds are not published through session/event; firstLiveSeq records the constructor boundary, and announce publishes session/created only after the seeded Session is entered. The core lifecycle therefore has the information needed for an explicit initial-state handoff, but the current event payload does not carry it to projection owners.

The registry already owns restore and hydrate. They consume an explicit event cut and checkpoint, fold synchronously over supplied data, and install detached state without reading Session history themselves.

The projection cache is a fold shortcut and adapter: it supplies explicit cold events to hydrate/restore and persists checkpoints. It does not own live Session history and must not become a dependency of the core projection registry.

session-projection depends on the core Session package and is imported by session-query for projection types; importing session-query into session-projection would reverse the package direction and create a cycle.

decision.selected: Keep SessionProjectionRegistry as the sole owner of projection cells, watermarks, eager current-event drive, and synchronous state reads. Migrate its three history reads only after core Session lifecycle exposes an explicit initial-state handoff and the projection owner can require a supplied baseline. Use the existing restore/hydrate methods for prepared or cold cuts; do not make the registry discover history through SessionQuery or SQLite.
owner_rules: A projection unit may apply only the committed event delivered by the Session lifecycle or an explicit event cut supplied to restore/hydrate.
The registry must not create a missing cell by calling snapshotEvents() or advance a cell by calling eventAt() once the lifecycle handoff is available.

stateOf(), snapshot(), and checkpoint() remain synchronous after a cell has an exact baseline and watermark; a missing or stale baseline must fail explicitly instead of folding an implicit history read.
A late registration or a seeded/resumed Session requires an explicit adoption step before host state is read. Registration must not silently substitute init state or discard the inherited prefix.
decision.next_seam: Specify a core Session/SessionStore lifecycle handoff for the exact constructor seed or prepared cut, including existing-session registration and disposal ordering. The handoff is an initialization delivery, not a general arbitrary-history reader: it is available at Session publication/adoption and is not retained as a new public snapshot alias.
decision.cache_and_cold: Keep session-projection-cache as the storage adapter. Its cold read obtains the required event slice and calls restore; a prepared observation calls hydrate. A cache row remains a fold shortcut, never an authoritative live state source.
decision.dependency_boundary: session-projection remains independent of session-query, session-query-sqlite, persistence implementations, and storage backends. Query consumers may use projection state, but projection initialization does not call back into query.
decision.retained_until: REM-028-S067-069 remain line-scoped retained owner exceptions until the core lifecycle handoff and projection baseline precondition are implemented and verified. No new production call to a deprecated Session reader is permitted.

acceptance_for_follow_up: A fresh Session initializes every registered unit at cursor -1 and continues through delivered events without a history lookup.
A seeded or restored Session receives its exact constructor/prepared cut, including inheritedEventCount and the end-seed marker when present, before any projection consumer reads state.
A unit registered after a Session exists is explicitly hydrated or rejected with a named missing-baseline error; it never silently folds Session history.
A delivered event cannot advance a cell across a missing sequence; the owner reports the missing baseline instead of reading an arbitrary position.
restore/hydrate, checkpoint, projection-cache cold reads, HMR disposal, late registration, fork cuts, and change notifications preserve their current state, watermark, and lifecycle semantics.

Focused registry and projection-cache tests prove complete removal of S067-S069, and the candidate-bound deprecated-reader and suppression metrics decrease without a global lint or compiler relaxation.
rejected: Import session-query or SQLite into session-projection: this creates a dependency cycle and makes a synchronous lifecycle owner depend on an asynchronous query service.
Route raw projection initialization through SessionQuery: this conflates query observations with projection state, adds persistence availability to the core seam, and changes sdk-minimal composition.
Make ProjectionDefinition.apply async: event publication and client snapshots are synchronous, so an async fold would break event ordering and the current watermark/change-feed guarantees.
Delete lazy registration behavior without an explicit lifecycle baseline: late plugin activation and seeded/resumed Sessions would either lose state or fail at an unrelated consumer read.
Remove the line-scoped waivers without the owner seam and focused equivalence tests: a lower count would not prove correct fork, resume, HMR, or late-registration behavior.
retained_exceptions: REM-028-S067, REM-028-S068, and REM-028-S069 remain in packages/session/session-projection/src/index.ts under their existing local migration waivers.
A10 changes no production source, package metadata, Session format generation, persistence schema, wire version, candidate tree, or public composition.
The sealed A28 candidate remains unchanged; any implementation requires a successor rebuild and requalification.
limitations: A10 is a source-grounded design action; the core lifecycle handoff is not yet implemented.
The current worktree still lacks the 12 tracked paths required by the canonical audit-metrics command; candidate-bound metric promotion remains a later successor check.
No publication, registry, push, merge, release, or final-verdict action was taken.
decision_summary: Accept the projection-owner design. Keep the registry synchronous and independent, use explicit restore/hydrate cuts, and retain S067-S069 only until a core lifecycle adoption seam can supply a complete baseline without a new arbitrary-history alias.
